title: Money Roadmap
l1d: Everything starts with knowing where your money goes. A simple guide: half for needs, thirty percent for wants, and twenty percent for saving and paying debt.
l2d: Before attacking debt, build a small cushion of one thousand dollars, or one month of expenses if that is lower, so surprises do not push you back into debt.
l3d: Put every extra dollar on your debts. Snowball pays the smallest balance first for quick wins. Avalanche pays the highest interest first and usually saves the most money.
l4d: Grow your cushion to three months of expenses. This is your safety net if you lose income.
l5d: Now save for what matters to you: a trip, a course, a vehicle. Set a goal amount above and watch it fill.
l6d: With a safety net and no costly debt, you can start investing. Beginners often choose low-cost diversified index funds, add money every month, and think in decades, not days.
l7d: Time is your biggest ally. Move the sliders to see how monthly contributions grow with compound interest.
nosurplus: You need income above expenses to get there.
